summary: First engineering-value experiment (EV1), off-chain public synthetic DEVELOPMENT evidence. A versioned Engineering Value Contract freezes a battery decision: choose from 16 two-stage charge protocols the one reaching constant-voltage onset soonest, subject to reach, plating and peak-temperature constraints across every condition of a scenario, with provisional DEVELOPMENT preferences and evidence-derived reference uncertainty bands. Each model makes the same deterministic selection from its own predictions; Carbon verifies it against pinned-PyBaMM references, reporting regret to the best in the tested set, improvement over the baseline, false acceptance/rejection, abstention, ranking and seed variation, and compares scoring rules (the approved control, 0/30/70 and sensitivities; 45/30/25 reported not measurable because battery has no defensible physics score) by rank agreement with decision quality, choosing on development scenarios and assessing on fresh verification scenarios. Zero weights use a separate versioned DEVELOPMENT profile; the core Score Pack is unchanged. No testnet rule, reward, chain action or spend changes. Authentic run (2026-09-25): 384 pinned-PyBaMM references OK, 11 reconstructed members plus 5 synthetic controls. The approved rule is chosen on development and gives Kendall tau 0.165 on verification, against 0.110 for every reweighting: a weak, indicative preference for better decisions. The tested design set leaves the verification scenarios without a feasible protocol, and an error-accurate boundary-optimist control ranks above every reconstructed member. EV2 (a wider frozen design set) and a decision-aware robustness factor are recommended. Evidence is in docs/development/evidence/ev1-2026-09-25.
